anti_overlap: fd-emergent-narrative-design-legibility covers whether the resulting dynamics are interesting and legible to a player — this agent covers only whether the calibration methodology itself (sample size, identifiability, reference-class grounding, sequencing) is scientifically sound, independent of gameplay feel.

fd-bench-policy-discriminative-validity covers whether the calibrated simulation serves ShadowBench's alignment-evaluation and cross-policy discrimination purpose — this agent covers general ABM calibration validity, not bench-specific reproducibility or discriminative-power requirements.
decision_lens: Prioritizes findings where the calibration brief's own evidence or reasoning contains a methodological gap that would be invisible to a game-design review but is a known failure pattern in ABM/complex-systems calibration — e.g., tuning to hit a qualitative target (Warning band) without an identifiability check (are there many parameter combinations that produce the same steady-state band but different transient dynamics, and does the brief distinguish between them), or declaring success from a 4-seed sample when seed-to-seed variance at N=4 cannot statistically distinguish 'well-calibrated stochastic diversity' from 'overfit to these four particular seeds'. Deprioritizes findings purely about game feel or bench-discrimination.
focus: Whether the proposed calibration methodology (a parameter sweep against 4 seeds' cat_share curves, targeting a Warning-band no-shock steady state, per the jackpot-calibration-brief) is methodologically sound as a calibration exercise for a complex-systems / agent-based model — judged against computational social science and ABM calibration practice: identifiability, overfitting to a tiny seed sample, confusing 'passes a diagnostic' with 'matches a reference class', and the risk of tuning parameters to produce a desired qualitative outcome (seed variance) rather than validating against any external ground truth
name: fd-simulation-calibration-validity-methodology
persona: Apply the perspective of a computational social scientist / agent-based-modeling methodologist who calibrates complex socio-economic simulations against real-world reference classes (e.g., crisis base rates, GDP volatility, conflict-onset statistics) — someone trained to distrust a calibration that is validated only against the model's own internal diagnostics (does the curve spread?) rather than against any external target distribution, who knows that a handful of seeds is not a sample size that can distinguish a genuinely well-calibrated stochastic attractor from a lucky sweep result, and who treats 'the demographics→unrest feed injects more than decay removes at every level' as a classic sign of a badly conditioned dynamical system (a runaway positive-feedback ratchet) that a single decay/growth retune may only partially fix rather than structurally resolve.
review_areas: Identifiability: the brief proposes retuning 'per-tick decay and/or scale down intrinsic growth and the demographics→unrest conversion' to hit a target steady-state band, but multiple distinct parameter combinations can produce the same steady-state value with very different transient/shock-response dynamics (fast-decay/fast-growth vs slow-decay/slow-growth can both average to the same band) — verify whether the brief's recommended sweep distinguishes between these regimes, since they will respond completely differently to the seed-varied slow forcing that Option B2 proposes adding later, meaning A and B2 are not actually separable work items methodologically even though the brief sequences them as independent

Sample size and overfitting: the diagnosis and the implied validation both rest on 4 seeds (4242, 777, 1, 31337) — 4 seeds is not enough to establish that a retuned steady-state band produces genuinely seed-dependent T₀ rather than a still-narrow distribution that happens to look spread across this particular small sample; flag whether the successor bead's calibration-sweep plan (§6: 'N seeds × ~80-year runs') specifies an N large enough to make a distributional claim, or whether it will re-use the same small-N eyeball-the-curve methodology that produced the original bit-identical-collapse blind spot in the first place

External reference-class grounding (or its absence): the brief calibrates against the model's own internal diagnostic (cat_share curve shape, T₀ location) with zero external validation against real-world crisis base rates, onset-timing distributions, or comparable ABM/CSS literature on cascading-failure systems — this is the same category of gap PHILOSOPHY.md's 'honest simulation' principle warns against for gameplay tuning, but here it's a scientific-validity gap: a policy-fidelity claim ('base rates that match the reference class of real-world crises', per the target question's own stated tension) cannot be assessed at all under the current evidence, since no reference class appears anywhere in the brief's methodology

Runaway positive-feedback diagnosis vs. point-fix: the mechanism section (§2) shows demographics→unrest and intrinsic economic-strain growth 'out-inject decay at every pressure level' — this is evidence of a structurally unstable dynamical system (positive feedback dominates the linear/decay term across the entire operating range), which typically cannot be fixed by a single global retune of decay/growth constants without either (a) making the system stable everywhere (risking the brief's own named over-damping failure) or (b) leaving a narrow, fragile operating window that re-saturates under any calibration drift; check whether Option A's framing ('retune so no-shock steady state sits in Warning band') treats this as fixable by constant-tuning when the underlying structure may need a nonlinear correction (e.g., saturating conversion functions) to be robust

Confound between fixing the RNG-wiring bug (§3: seeded emergence RNG isn't reached by the CLI seed) and fixing the calibration (§1–§2): the brief's own §3 shows that TODAY's 4-seed 'seed-driven differences' (engine GDP trajectories, scripted-player deployments) are noise on top of a completely deterministic emergence layer — meaning the diagnostic evidence used to characterize the collapse mechanism (§2's attribution deltas) was itself gathered from a system where emergence-side stochasticity literally cannot vary; verify the successor calibration-sweep plan re-runs the §2 mechanism analysis AFTER B1 (seed-wiring fix) lands, rather than calibrating Option A's constants against attribution evidence gathered under an emergence RNG that was frozen the whole time

Validation criterion ambiguity: nowhere in the brief is there a stated quantitative pass/fail bar for 'the calibration is done' beyond qualitative language ('Warning band', 'requires compounding seeded shocks') — for a methodologist this is a red flag: without a pre-registered target metric (e.g., 'T₀ distribution across N=30 seeds has coefficient of variation > X and inter-seed leading-family Jaccard < Y'), the sweep-and-eyeball process described in §4 is vulnerable to the calibrator stopping as soon as the result looks plausible, which is exactly the failure mode that produced the original undiagnosed bit-identical collapse (it also looked plausible until someone ran the cross-seed diff)

severity_examples.condition: The new calibration passes the informal check, gets ruled and locked into the referee baseline, and 6–12 months later a wider seed sample (or a playtester) reveals the 'fixed' system still collapses via a narrow attractor band — a second full re-baseline cycle is required, repeating the exact failure pattern (undiagnosed narrow-attractor collapse validated by small-sample eyeballing) that this calibration effort exists to fix
severity_examples.scenario: The successor calibration-sweep bead runs Option A's retune and validates using the same small-N (4–8 seed), no-pre-registered-metric, eyeball-the-cat_share-curve methodology implied by the current brief

severity_examples.condition: B1 changes which emergence RNG streams actually fire (previously frozen), which changes the relative magnitude of the pressure-injection terms A is retuning against; the Option A constants, calibrated pre-B1, are silently miscalibrated post-B1, and nothing in the brief's plan re-validates A's constants after B1 lands because the recommendation frames them as two independent, parallelizable work items rather than a sequential dependency
severity_examples.scenario: Option A's constants are retuned and calibrated against attribution evidence from §2, which was gathered before B1 (seed-wiring fix) lands — but B1 is sequenced as a near-simultaneous prerequisite in the same recommendation (§4: 'B1 immediately + A as the core work')

severity_examples.condition: The retune achieves the Warning-band steady state at default conditions but the underlying linear ratchet structure remains, so scenario-mode starts (which deliberately pre-elevate specific pressures per VISION.md) push the same countries back into the same runaway regime the retune was meant to eliminate, because the fix was calibrated against a no-shock/default-start baseline that scenario mode does not represent
severity_examples.scenario: The brief's demographics→unrest and intrinsic-growth terms are retuned via global linear decay/growth-constant adjustment (the most natural reading of §4's 'raise per-tick decay and/or scale down intrinsic growth')

success_hints: The successor bead's calibration-sweep plan states a pre-registered, quantitative pass criterion (not just 'spread the curve') before the sweep runs, and specifies N large enough to support a distributional claim rather than a 4-seed eyeball check.
The plan explicitly sequences B1 (RNG wiring fix) strictly before Option A's constants are calibrated, and re-runs the §2-style attribution analysis post-B1 rather than reusing pre-B1 evidence.

The brief or its successor acknowledges whether any external reference class (real-world crisis onset/base-rate data, comparable ABM calibration literature) is being used to ground the target steady-state band, or explicitly scopes that grounding as future work rather than silently omitting it.

The identifiability question (do multiple decay/growth combinations hit the same steady-state band with different transient behavior) is at least named as a risk, even if not fully resolved before the ruling.
task_context: Design inquiry: gameplay interestingness vs scientific/policy simulation validity for shadow-work's civilizational sim, at its live calibration decision point. Reviewing the jackpot-calibration-brief's proposed methodology (parameter sweep targeting a qualitative Warning-band steady state, validated against 4 seeds' cat_share curves) against agent-based-model / computational-social-science calibration practice. Overall generative goal for this review round: maximize verified novelty×risk surface until dry — answering: what makes for the most interesting gameplay + scientific/policy simulation validity/fidelity for shadow-work?
